title: After Charm moves an ENEMY unit onto an uncontrolled battlefield, the Contested status is attributed to the spell's caster (player-1) instead of the moved unit's controller (player-2). Root: pending-choice.ts choose-destination branch calls markContestedOnArrival(draft, targetZoneId, choice.playerId) (and move.ts:220 uses ctx.playerId) — the chooser, not the unit's controller.
expected: Charm ("Move an enemy unit.") parses to {type:"move", target:{controller:"enemy"}, to:"choose"}. abilities/effects/move.ts:256-261 sets pendingChoice {type:"choose-destination", playerId: ctx.playerId} (the caster). On resolution, game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:876 calls markContestedOnArrival(draft, targetZoneId, choice.playerId), and move.ts:15-29 writes bf.contestedBy = playerId (and gates on bf.controller === playerId) using that caster id rather than the moved unit's controller. Same pattern at move.ts:220 with ctx.playerId. This violates rule 450 ("Contested ... by the controller of the Unit that moved"), so an enemy unit moved by Charm attributes contestedBy to player-1, matching the observed showdown/focus misattribution.
observed: battlefields['player-2-bf-ogn-276-298'] = {contested:true, contestedBy:'player-1', controller:null}; startShowdown offered to player-1; showdown opened with attackingPlayer:'player-1', focusPlayer:'player-1', isCombatShowdown:true although player-1 has no units there; after both players passed focus the battlefield remained {contested:true, contestedBy:'player-1', controller:null, showdownComplete:true} (player-2 never got control) and a bogus resolveFullCombat move was then offered at a battlefield holding only player-2's Recruit; endTurn was not offered.

history.note: contestedBy already attributed to arriving unit's controller; tightened Charm regression to assert P2 ends up controlling bf2

resolution.note: contestedBy already attributed to arriving unit's controller; tightened Charm regression to assert P2 ends up controlling bf2
